links.comparator_used: Higher-quality reference standard outcome data combining EMR and cancer registry, used to validate the same survival models
links.outcome: Model performance estimates (discrimination via C-index, integrated Brier score, calibration) when validating with EMR follow-up data alone versus EMR plus registry data
links.effect: All-features model: C-index 0.67 (95% CI, 0.65 to 0.69) and IBS 0.16 (95% CI, 0.15 to 0.17) with EMR only, versus C-index 0.66 (95% CI, 0.65 to 0.68) and IBS 0.17 (95% CI, 0.16 to 0.18) with reference standard data. With fewer features, performance estimates dropped similarly in both scenarios. The model was reasonably calibrated against the reference standard, but EMR-only data wrongly showed systematic underprediction of survival.
links.tradeoff: EMR data undercapture deaths, causing informative censoring. This led to a false conclusion of miscalibration (survival underprediction).
links.quote: EMR data were useful for validation of model discrimination, but not calibration.

design_hint: Local validation of deployed model using EMR-only follow-up data versus registry-linked reference data
